newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex's Lajous sees LPG subsidy gone by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Pemex's Lajous sees LPG subsidy gone by year-end.

text.p: Mexico's government subsidies on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) should be removed by the fourth quarter, state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) chairman Adrian Lajous said on Tuesday.

"Given normal seasonal effects and forecasts...it should be in the second half, probably the fourth quarter," Lajous told a news conference, referring to when the fuel's price would level with natural market prices.
He added that Pemex would provide technical support to help with the transition from administered prices to freed prices, at the government's request.
Government officials had estimated that a gradual reduction of the subsidy of about 2.5 percent per month would remove the government's support of LPG by July.
LPG is commonly used in Mexican households with domestic sales at about 265,000 barrels per day in 1996.
The removal of the LPG subsidy is expected to encourage the use of cleaner natural gas and help Mexico comply with new, more rigorous air quality standards.
Companies interested in natural gas distribution tenders have complained that the subsidy stifles interest in natural gas and suggested the government has dragged its heels on removing the subsidy.
Higher LPG prices have already been factored into Banco de Mexico's 15 percent inflation forecast for 1997.
